section_1.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Change
section_1.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as 'instantaneous rate of change' (the slope of a tangent line) and the integral as 'accumulation' (the area under a curve). Use a visual analogy of a car's speedometer vs. its odometer.
section_1.example: Visualize a robotic turtle moving. The derivative is how fast the turtle moves at a specific tick; the integral is the total path length the turtle has covered over time.

section_2.title: The Core Connection: Inverse Operations
section_2.content: Explain that differentiation and integration are inverse processes, much like addition and subtraction or multiplication and division. Introduce the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1) visually by showing a dynamic rectangle sweeping out an area.
section_2.example: Imagine a stack of paper sheets. The derivative tells you the thickness of a single sheet; the integral tells you the total height of the stack.

section_3.title: Visual Proof: The Accumulation Function
section_3.content: Display an animation of a function f(t). As a vertical line moves across the x-axis, show the area accumulating as a shaded region. Graphically demonstrate how the derivative of this 'area function' maps back to the original function value.
section_3.example: A smart-sensor drone monitoring the density of a forest canopy: The accumulation function tracks total biomass as the drone flies forward; the derivative reveals the biomass density at any specific coordinate.

section_4.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_4.content: Reinforce the 'Fundamental Bridge' concept: If you differentiate an integral, you return to the starting point. Highlight that this relationship allows us to calculate areas without infinite summation.
section_4.example: A recap animation showing a cycle: [Function] -> (Integrate) -> [Area Function] -> (Differentiate) -> [Back to Function]. It’s a closed-loop system!

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to give lecture space
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [

            "This provides a closed-loop system for calculus.", 
            "Area calculation is now simplified forever."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        f = MathTex("f(x)", color="#FFD700").scale(1.5)
        integral = MathTex(r"\int_a^x f(t) dt", color="#FFA500").scale(1.2)

        self.add(self.title)

        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
